body:
No method gives "near-certain profit" in stocks. What works is a repeatable process that tilts the odds in your favour, sizes positions so you survive being wrong, and holds the rare big winner long enough for it to compound. The base rates are harsh. **About 58% of US stocks returned less than one-month T-bills over their lifetimes, and about 4% of stocks created all the net wealth in the US market from 1926 to 2016** ([Bessembinder, JFE 2018](https://wpcarey.asu.edu/sites/default/files/2021-10/do-stocks-outperform-treasury-bills.pdf)). In India, **87.7–93% of individual F&O traders lost money in every year SEBI has studied** ([Business Standard](https://www.business-standard.com/markets/capital-market-news/sebi-study-exposes-massive-losses-for-individual-f-o-traders-in-india-124092400948_1.html); [Finnovate summary of SEBI FY26 study](https://www.finnovate.in/learn/blog/sebi-fno-trader-losses-fy26-individual-derivatives)). Across retail investors, legendary investors, professional firms and quants, the winning methods share one structure. Quality and growth filters decide *what* to own. A view that differs from consensus, together with a check on what the price already assumes, decides *why now*. Trend and regime filters decide *when*. Position-sizing rules decide *how much*. AI is now useful for the reading-heavy middle of that pipeline: summarising filings, red-teaming a thesis and screening for forensic problems. The evidence that AI can *pick* stocks on its own is weak to negative. Live LLM trading contests mostly lost money, and the oldest AI-run ETF has trailed the S&P 500. One correction to the starting story is needed. Radico Khaitan did rise roughly 25–90x depending on the entry point, but it went sideways for **eight years after 2008**. The move began in **2016–17**, driven by premiumisation, debt reduction and operating leverage. No 2008 "UBL issue" caused it. This report is educational and is not personalised financial advice.

title: AI stock picking playbook › Trade Certainty for Edge: Multibagger Playbook

body:
| # | Signal to look for | Where to find it | Case example |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | A small, fast segment hidden inside a big, flat company | Segment notes, investor decks | NVIDIA data center FY16–18; Royal Enfield inside Eicher |
| 2 | Mix shift → gross margin → operating leverage | Concall commentary on mix, A&P spend | Radico revenue +44% → PAT +239% |
| 3 | Balance-sheet inflection (deleveraging, capex cycle ending) | Cash-flow statement, debt schedule | Radico D/E 0.77 → 0.15 |
| 4 | Policy documents that come before order books | Budget, PLI notifications, import lists | Defence, EMS |
| 5 | Competitor distress or industry structure change | News, channel checks, dealer and shelf visits | USL turmoil (unverified as a contemporaneous thesis); wind consolidation |
| 6 | Capacity utilisation >80% plus a brownfield expansion | Concalls, investor presentations | Deepak phenol |
| 7 | Promoter behaviour: buying, no pledge, refusing to dilute cheaply | SAST/PIT disclosures, shareholding pattern | Radico promoter refusing Mallya |
| 8 | A starting valuation that leaves room for rerating | P/E against own history and peers; reverse DCF | Radico (both engines) vs defence 2025 (rerating already spent) |

Fisher's **"scuttlebutt"** means talking to customers, suppliers, competitors and ex-employees. It is the original way to validate a mind-map node ([Fisher, *Common Stocks and Uncommon Profits*, primary text not re-fetched]). Professionals add paid alternative data such as card transactions and web scraping. Hedge funds are the largest buyers of alternative data, at about 55–68% of the market ([GM Insights](https://gminsights.com/industry-analysis/alternative-data-market)). Retail cannot match that, but free proxies cover much of the ground. In India these include monthly auto sales, GST and power data, concall transcripts, Google Trends, app rankings and job postings. Bulk and block deal data, monthly mutual-fund portfolio disclosures and quarterly shareholding patterns also give Indian investors unusually good visibility into what institutions are doing ([EquityResearchIndia](https://www.equityresearchindia.com/post/block-deals-and-bulk-deals-how-to-track-big-institutional-trades-and-what-they-signal); [SEBI](https://www.sebi.gov.in/legal/circulars/mar-2009/circular-portfolio-format-for-debt-oriented-close-ended-and-interval-schemes-plans_14185.html)). Treat superinvestor tracking as an idea source, never as conviction. US 13F filings arrive up to 45 days late, and research suggests much of the "superstar" alpha is earned before the filing becomes public ([Christoffersen et al.](https://www.bwl.uni-mannheim.de/media/Lehrstuehle/bwl/Area_Finance/Finance_Area_Seminar/HWS2018/Christoffersen_Paper.pdf); [InvestorLens](https://www.investorlens.capital/docs/faq/can-filings-predict-performance)).

The public **"Coffee Can Investing"** Screener screen requires average ROCE and ROE above 14% across 10/7/5/3-year windows, sales growth above 9%, D/E below 1 and pledge below 15%. It returned about 100 names in November 2026 and is a good template to clone ([Screener](https://www.screener.in/screens/1125448/coffee-can-investing/)). For technical gating, ready-made Minervini Trend Template scans exist for India ([MarketInOut](https://www.marketinout.com/stock-screener/minervini-trend-template/india)).

data.section: Screener.in starting queries

title: AI stock picking playbook › Screener.in starting queries

body:
- The visible winners are a biased sample. Founders hold one concentrated asset that they *control and operate*. Public-market investors who copy that concentration lack the control and the information, and add leverage. The leveraged, concentrated copycats go bust and drop off the lists, so nobody sees them.
- Rich-list "finance" fortunes come mainly from asset-management *businesses*: fees on other people's capital, scale, and franchise. That is itself a founder or owner route, not personal stock-picking returns.
- SEBI's FY26 finding (losses fall as equity holdings rise) suggests capital base and experience shape outcomes, not just knowledge. Selection effects may also explain it.

data.section: Inferences

title: knowledge_vs_outcomes › Inferences

body: Veliyath's audited-style PMS series (from his firm's own site) shows a genuine long-run edge in small caps, including big wins in FY14–FY17 and FY21. It also shows a catastrophic two-year drawdown: FY19 -31.87% and FY20 -51.48%, about -67% compounded, while the Nifty 50 TRI was roughly -13% over the same two years. That loss was partly self-admitted ("chor" stock bets, the LEEL Electricals misjudgement). An investor who entered at the FY18 peak was roughly back to breakeven only by end-FY22. I found no SEBI enforcement order against him for front-running or manipulation; the only SEBI order naming him is a 2009 consent (settlement) order in a Geojit Securities matter whose terms I could not read.

title: porinju_prsundar › Takeaway

body:
`insight:indian-ipo-long-run-returns` | confidence: verified | date: 2026-11-19

Evidence (different samples, so treat ranges, not points). (1) Tracker marketping.in (methodology: issue price to latest close; accessed Nov 2026; single-source): mainboard share trading below issue - 2021 44.4% (median +24.8%), 2022 42.9% (+25.9%), 2023 42.4% (+33.0%), 2024 49.5% (median 0.0%), 2025 48.1% (+1.9%); SME - 2023 48.9% (+9.8%), 2024 58.3% (median -20.4%), 2025 56.6% (-11.5%). (2) Economic Times analysis cited by Share India (2026): over 51% of 155 large IPOs (Rs500cr+) listed 2023-25 were below issue price, several 50-70% off debut levels. (3) Client Associates 'New-Age IPO Performance Analysis' (25 VC/PE-backed listings May-2020 to Jun-2025, vs BSE 500, as of 16 Jun 2025): average subscription 48.5x; 17 of 25 had listing gains averaging 24.15%, yet only 36% of IPO-price buyers and 32% of post-listing buyers earned positive alpha (43% of pre-IPO investors). (4) SEBI flipping study (separate record): most allottees exit within a week. Pattern: the median mainboard IPO roughly matches or slightly lags the market over 1-3 years, a minority of big winners lifts the average, and buying on listing day (after the pop) is the worst entry. Issues during hot windows (2021, 2024) fare worst. Consistent with Buffett's 2000 'wealth transfer' warning and global IPO-underperformance literature. Actionable: default answer to any IPO is 'not now'; revisit after 4-8 quarters of listed results unless we have a genuine information edge.

**L5 parent-take table (v1.1), for MNC subsidiaries and group companies.** By year: royalty (rate × eligible base); technical, support and cost-allocation fees; reimbursements paid and received; purchases from group companies (share of purchases) with the pricing formula; sales to group companies (share of revenue, share of exports) with the pricing formula; dividends to the parent; and stock-based pay in *parent* shares. **S2 checklist (v1.3, before L1; ~1 hour).** Fill every disqualifier-v2 rule as pass / fail / unknown with a dated
source *before* starting the layers, so the card never shows "incomplete" (H3 was never checked in the first three
practice runs). Hard at entry: H1a, H1b, H1c, H2, H3, H4, H5. Hard at exit: auditor exit on denied information,
RBI divergence, US 8-K 4.02, results delayed past the deadline. Graded: pledge (>25%, escalate >50% or rising),
accounting-trouble events in 5 years, dilution (price × purpose × buyer), debtor days by counterparty, solvency set.
Questions only: CFO/PAT, negative FCF, other-income share. Sources: `nse_fetch.py announcements/pledge/shareholding/
integrated`, `bse_fetch.py announcements` (catches Reg-30 items the NSE description hides), rating letters, the AR
auditor's report and notes. Lenders: use the bank form of each rule (adaptation section).

**L8 valuation and decision (v1.3; from `research_notes/Templates/valuation_and_decision.md` §5).**
1. Collect the extra inputs the templates need: a **dated close from two sources**, **10 FY-end P/Es (P/B for
   lenders)** for the own-history band, **3+ peer P/Es (P/Bs)**, **6-month ADV**, net cash/debt or (lenders) book
   and pending dilution, and the explicit S2 statuses.
2. Write the scenarios (growth/margin/ROIIC/exit P/E, or ROE path/exit P/B) and probabilities **before** reading the
   price outputs; anchor on the base-rate class first.
3. Run the worksheet; read (a) implied growth or ROE and the base-case IRR, (b) exit multiple vs the DCF/RIM-consistent
   multiple (the hidden bet, L21), (c) re-rating share, (d) temperature vs own history and peers, (e) sensitivity.
4. Fill the card from the deep dive: S2 statuses, PEAD quintile and event date, credibility **with peer median**,
   detector alerts, the L7 override table, base-rate class, sizing tier, dated kill criteria, pre-mortem, review date.
5. Run the card with `--calls`. Practice runs: paper calls tagged `practice-example`, **not ingested** (L21).
6. Write the variant view or accept size 0: ≥3 open soft flags without one blocks the card.

data.section: Commands

title: README › Commands

body:
- Frame (`s1_frame.py`): every company on BSE's Active (5,138 fetched 22-Nov-2026), Delisted (4,624) and Suspended
  (1,238) scrip lists, NSE-only active symbols (EQUITY_L), and IBBI / NSE-delisting rows with an NSE symbol but no BSE
  code (from `research_notes/Universe/india_dead_companies_2026-11-22.csv`). One row per company (ISIN > BSE code > NSE
  symbol). 221 IBBI rows with no exchange identifier (renamed companies; name did not match) cannot be fetched —
  counted in the survivorship audit.
- **Strata** (stratified sample, the brief allows it when the full universe is too large):
  - **D — distress lists, census (1,739 companies, all fetched):** IBBI CIRP / liquidation / NCLT rows, NSE
    compulsory or liquidation delisting, NSE suspension, BSE suspended list.
  - **X — BSE/NSE delisted, not D (2,132; random sample 500, seed 20161, weight 4.264):** mergers, voluntary
    delistings, old exits, reason unknown.
  - **L — live, not D (5,070; random sample 900, seed 20161, weight 5.633):** on BSE or NSE active lists today.
  All statistics are **weighted by stratum weight** (population / sample) so they estimate the full frame.
- Membership at T: a screener page; FY0 exists as above; a price observation within 31 days before T; size known.
- **Size:** market cap at T = screener market-cap-to-sales at the last weekly price ≤ T × trailing-12-month sales
  (last value dated ≤ T). Keep **₹200 cr ≤ mcap ≤ ₹20,000 cr**. Market-cap-to-sales comes rounded to 0.1, so the
  band uses the point estimate; rows whose ±0.05 rounding interval straddles a boundary are counted as
  "ambiguous size" and reported. Zero or missing sales ⇒ size unknown ⇒ excluded and counted.
- Exclude financials (`solvency_screen.is_financial`: banks, NBFCs, insurers, brokers, housing finance — they need
  an ALM test).
- Exclude companies **already in insolvency at T** (IBBI CIRP admission or liquidation dated ≤ T) and count them.
- One row per (company, snapshot); CIs are bootstrapped by company within stratum.

Indian annual-report pilot (pre-registered, 200 firms incl. later-dead, FY22→23/FY23→24): MD&A and auditor+CARO
big-change quintiles −2.1% / −0.8% vs sector-size controls (t ≈ −0.3/−0.1); new adverse auditor item +7.7% (wrong

+ CARO vs last year stays a deep-dive judgment cue (worst cases −42% to −77%, but big winners too).

Indian promoter buying, PEAD long leg, Lazy Prices US v1/v2, India AR text. Edge is likelier in human-depth work
(promise tracking, deep dives) combined with the few proven filters than in mechanical text/flow signals.

title: lessons › L32 (2026-11-23) — Text change fails in India too; signal-test scorecard 1 of 7

body:
**Stage 3 and survival**
8. **Both-flags balance-sheet question (L39, L39 addendum).** One red flag (pledge > 25% of promoter holding or interest cover < 1.5x) outside the PEAD window → starter size ≤ 1%, no additions (card v1.3). Both flags → 12-month halving 4.2×, 3-yr failure 9.4× (stable across periods). Write the balance-sheet answer (debt maturity, refinancing source, covenant headroom, pledge lender and trigger price) **before** even a starter position. This is a judgement rule until the pre-registered "both flags → 0 new money" test runs.
9. **Credibility power (L49).** Report the number of scored past promises. Fewer than 10 → label the score "under-powered (n = k)": it moves at most ±0.10 from the sector base rate. Score numbers and dates separately (L44: SHK missed both). Score guidance on items the company excludes from "adjusted" profit as its own category (L53: VIYASH's ESOP-cost guide missed ~3×).

**Government inputs and external facts**
10. **Government / licence / lease inputs (L40, L42).** List every government-granted or government-priced input: land lease, mining lease, licence, spectrum, PPP/concession, subsidised financing, interest subsidy, PLI, policy-dated rules (e.g. solar ALMM relaxations). For each, record the expiry, the obligation given in return and compliance with it, the counterparty's own filings, and whether the AR mentions it. An expired or contested input → `survival.core_asset_threat` on the card (card v1.4), and the stock is valued as an option on renewal.
11. **External facts absent from the AR (L40, L41, L42, L45).** Search news, court records, gazettes and counterparty filings for the key asset. Any material fact the AR, deck or calls do not mention becomes a disclosure flag and an L7 row (INDRAMEDCO lease expiry, Utkarsh's Bihar MFI Act, HARSHA's subsidy-backed debt, UTTAMSUGAR's ethanol-tender exclusion).
12. **State-law check above 15% concentration (L41).** For any state above ~15% of the loan book, revenue, capacity or cane/raw-material area, search that state's gazette and assembly records for laws, ordinances and tariff orders on the activity. Record each with its date.
13. **Administered-price calendar (L45).** For every administered or government-set price (cane SAP/FRP, sugar MSP, export quota, ethanol tender design, power tariff order, DPCO/NLEM ceiling, excise, gas APM, freight), keep a table: last value + date, next decision date, sensitivity (₹ per unit → % of EBITDA), and whether the company's latest filing mentions it. A partial withdrawal of an input goes into the tails with a written note, because the card's core-asset trigger is yes/no.
